correctness.rationale: The all-fixed-length exposure lemma is established on each connected component: a cyclic component has v<=e; a tree with e<=2ell-4 has a center with eccentricity<=ell-2 and hence at least one unexposed vertex, so a_ell<=e; a tree with e>=2ell-3 has at most e+1<=((2ell-2)/(2ell-3))e exposed vertices. Long paths with 2ell-2 vertices attain equality. The universal conditional success hazard is bounded by ((2ell-2)/(2ell-3))j/n; reserved path templates attain the bound up to O(1) expected wastage, yielding the uniform O_{ell,L}(n^-1/2) survival asymptotics. No uniformity in ell growing with n is claimed; the proof addresses every fixed ell>=3. Independent graph and path-instance checks passed.

originality.rationale: The ell=3 triangle instance is known in the published same-day triangle result and is expressly not claimed new. For every ell>=4, the full sharp coefficient (ell-1)/(2ell-3), the componentwise exposure extremal lemma, and a matching adaptive path-template strategy go beyond the inspected fixed-subgraph threshold literature. The distinct general theorem is not implied by triangle alone. This is a best-of-knowledge originality assessment, not absolute priority certification.

value.rationale: Generalizing one target to every fixed simple cycle is a natural graph-process classification, not an arbitrary subcase. The sharp ((2ell-2)/(2ell-3)) exposed-vertices/edge extremum explains and quantifies the optimal first-cycle time for each length; a single constructive algorithm attains the exact full constant-probability window. Such constants and laws are genuine additional information beyond a mere sqrt(n) scale and can guide online subgraph construction analysis.

limitations: Fixed ell only; full choice of any other endpoint, independent offered vertices with replacement.
Historical priority is best-of-knowledge; finite enumeration only corroborates structural proof.
